brief: JPMorgan's positioning monitor finds bond markets bifurcated: quant funds (CTAs) built extreme short-duration bets that delivered 3-4% September returns, but their momentum signals hit extreme levels on September 30, risking profit-taking and mean reversion. Discretionary real-money managers, carrying an overhang of long duration and spread exposure built up in recent weeks, have been scrambling to cut it, pushing futures position proxies lower into end-September. JPMorgan's near-term bias favors continued discretionary deleveraging over a quant mean-reversion rally, given discretionary managers are larger. Separately, 2Q26 COFER data show FX reserve inflows of $80bn, with outflows from dollar ($15bn) and yen (~$40bn) reserves offset by $100bn into euro, resuming diversification paused in 1Q; the dollar's reserve share is projected to fall to 56.3% in 3Q while gold's share, after dipping to 28% on valuation, is projected to rise again. After Brazil's first election round, institutional positioning (EWZ short interest) stayed cautious even as retail EWZ buying and Ibovespa/BRL futures positioning rose. Digital-asset capital flow is running at a $66bn annualized pace, still half of last year's, with crypto ETF and futures positioning both rising in Q3, creating positive momentum into Q4.
